newsitem.title: USA: BPA hopes to develop market for "green" power.
newsitem.headline: BPA hopes to develop market for "green" power.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) hopes to develop a market for "green" power through a recently-announced alliance with the Environmental Resources Trust (ERT), a non-profit organization founded with support from the Environmental Defense Fund.

Dennis Oster, the BPA account executive in charge of the project, said Thursday the agency is committed to sell at least 15 megawatts (MW) of "environmentally beneficial" power this fiscal year (ending September 30), and the agreement could eventually result in sales of 200 MW a year or more.

The agency defines "environmentally beneficial" to include power produced as a side effect of the extra water moved through hydropower dams in order to aid fish migration, as well as power produced from renewable resources such as wind and geothermal plants.

BPA, a federal agency which markets hydro and nuclear power generated in the Pacific Northwest, currently has no wind or geothermal generation, but proceeds from the ERT alliance may be used to fund such investments in the future, Oster said.
BPA estimates about 129 average megawatt hours of hydropower are currently produced from federal dams as the result of fish-flow requirements.
That power is now "being dumped on spot markets as undifferentiated power," said Zak Willey, ERT pacific region director.
Additional unquantified volumes of electricity are generated when excess water is run through turbines in order to minimize dissolved gas levels in the streams.
ERT will donate the brokerage fee it receives from BPA and any price premium received from customers to various environmental programs, Willey said.
